span.label: why the agricultural collapse is self-reinforcing: about 70% of Ukraine's petrol and diesel came from Russia and Belarus, so the same conflict that closes the market also removes the fuel needed to plant, harvest and move what is left
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: why poultry and cattle recover on different clocks - a broiler is 21 days as an egg and 42 out of it, so flocks return within months of a maize harvest, while cattle take three or four years
span.term: biological recovery time as an economic constraint
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: why some shortfalls hurt and others do not: edible oils substitute for one another and store well, so removing the world's largest sunflower oil exporter is mostly a financial event; pharmaceuticals do not substitute, because labelling, dosage and formulary differ across borders
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the route from supply shock to food safety: shortage plus price spike plus substitution pressure creates the conditions for adulteration, and the paper names the four Ukrainian products most exposed - honey, sunflower oil, grains and seafood
span.term: scarcity as an opening for fraud
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the paper's conclusion from its own historical cases: absent large external investment of the kind that followed the Second World War, the economic damage outlasts the conflict by generations
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE PAPER GIVES UKRAINE'S CEREAL EXPORT RANK AS SECOND IN ONE SECTION AND FOURTH IN ANOTHER, both flatly and with different citations - a self-inconsistency in a headline figure, not a hedge
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the same divergence at smaller scale on wheat: 3.2% versus 3.3% of global production, 9.1% versus 9% of exports
span.note: about this quote: 2026-08-25 terminal-a. FLATTENED EXPONENT IN THIS QUOTE - THE NUMBER IS WRONG BY ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE AS IT STANDS. The staged text reads '18.06 × 106', where the paper writes 10 to the power 6. The superscript was pushed onto the line by the PDF extractor. The quote is verbatim to the staged text and its anchor is sound; the STAGED TEXT is what is damaged. NOT repaired - repair means re-staging the body and re-anchoring the record. Found by CLAUDE_B, row chk_flattened_exponent_in_a_quote.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the mechanism is in the methods and is not presented as a limitation: each impact area was searched by one co-author in their own area of expertise, corroborated by the others - a division of labour with no stated step for reconciling figures BETWEEN areas
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the scope is what thirteen experts ranked in the top six; sustainability was proposed and excluded, so an impact absent from this paper may have been considered and voted out rather than not existing
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: searches ran only from 13 March to 14 May 2022 - weeks into a war whose effects the paper repeatedly projects years forward
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: much of the evidence is grey literature by design, which the authors defend as necessary for a timely and evolving topic rather than treat as a weakness

span.label: food quality and safety had very little academic research behind them at the time of writing, so that section rests on analogy to Syria, Yemen and Chernobyl rather than on studies of this conflict
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: selecting the six impact areas by a two-round e-Delphi of 13 experts BEFORE the literature search, and reporting which candidate impacts did not make the top six
span.note: eliminates: the review's scope being set by what the authors happened to find - the selection is prior, structured, and its losers are named. It does NOT eliminate the panel being wrong about what would matter · outcome: partial

span.label: assigning each impact area to the co-author with expertise in it, with corroboration by the others
span.note: eliminates: one reviewer covering six specialist domains badly - AND IT IS ALSO THE CAUSE OF THE SECOND-VERSUS-FOURTH CONTRADICTION. The corroboration step operated within areas and evidently not across them · outcome: partial

span.label: a satellite Vegetation Condition Index comparison of March 2021 against March 2022, normalised against the historical NDVI range for the same period
span.note: eliminates: a claimed reduction in planting resting on reports from a war zone - the index is normalised to the same calendar window in a prior year, so seasonality is differenced out · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: stating explicitly where the impact will be SMALL - sunflower oil attenuated by fungibility, maize replaceable from three US states, poultry prices barely moved, pharmaceutical shortages minor against a $1.2 trillion market
span.note: eliminates: a catastrophe framing applied uniformly - the paper distinguishes what the world loses from what Ukraine loses, and says so in the sections where the answer is inconvenient to its own headline · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: using prior shocks with known outcomes as calibration - the 2007-08 food price crisis, Syria's 90% export collapse, Transnistria and South Ossetia's halved GDP, Bangladesh's 45-year recovery
span.note: eliminates: forecasts with no reference class; each projection is anchored to a case where the outcome is already known · outcome: held

span.label: noting that other recent wars - Tigray, Nagorno-Karabakh - were functionally invisible in global markets
span.note: eliminates: the assumption that any war disrupts global food supply; the claim is about THIS conflict's particular position in the trade network, and the counter-examples are named · outcome: held

span.label: wheat → food supply chains
span.note: TWO INCOMPATIBLE VALUES FOR ONE QUANTITY, INSIDE ONE PAPER. Ukraine is the SECOND largest cereal exporter in section 3.2.1 and the FOURTH largest in section 3.2.4, each stated flatly with its own citation. There is no relation type for `this record asserts X and also asserts not-X`, and no field on a content_tags row for `contradicted by another row in the same record`. The corpus can hold both numbers and cannot hold the fact that they disagree
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: e-Delphi → food supply chains
span.note: A METHOD THAT DETERMINES WHAT THE PAPER IS ABOUT. The panel's ranking did not measure the world; it selected which six impacts would be researched, and sustainability lost. That is a relation between a PROCEDURE and the SCOPE OF A CLAIM - not between two concepts in the world - and none of the eight types reaches it. It is the same gap as tsao2017's `maturity -> Ga2O3`: our vocabulary describes the world and cannot describe an appraisal or a choice about the world
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the six impact areas - CHOSEN BY VOTE BEFORE THE EVIDENCE WAS GATHERED. Thirteen experts proposed impacts in round one and ranked them in round two, and the TOP SIX became the paper's scope. Sustainability was named and did not make the cut. So the review's coverage is a measure of what a panel expected to matter in March 2022, not of what the literature contains
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Ukraine's rank as a cereal exporter, IN THIS PAPER - SECOND IN SECTION 3.2.1 AND FOURTH IN SECTION 3.2.4. Both are stated flatly, 16,000 characters apart, with different citations. Neither is hedged and neither refers to the other. A reader quoting `this paper says Ukraine is the Nth largest cereal exporter` can be right twice with different N
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the same divergence at a smaller scale, on wheat: production is 3.2% of global in one section and 3.3% in another, exports 9.1% and then 9%. Individually these are rounding; TOGETHER WITH THE RANK THEY ARE A PATTERN, and the methods section names the mechanism - one co-author per impact area, each searching independently
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: impact, as this paper uses it - A FORECAST FOR MOST OF THE SIX AREAS, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The searches ran 13 March to 14 May 2022, weeks into the war, so claims like the 2022 cattle slaughter, the 2023 meat shortfall and the recovery timescales are predictions stated in the present tense
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: food security, in the Ukrainian short term - ACCESS, NOT AVAILABILITY, and the paper is careful to separate them: stocks inside Ukraine were about 1.14 times annual demand. The shortage is of transport, fuel and labour rather than of food, which is why the mitigation list is about logistics
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → the 2007-2008 World Food Price Crisis, in which Ukraine's export tariffs removed over $300 million of wheat from world markets
span.note: and the comparison is used to argue the reference case UNDERSTATES the present one: the removal was a minor exacerbating factor then, and world dependence on Ukrainian cereals has grown since
